title: Shooting & Finishing Challenge
description: How sharp is your shooting and finishing?

questions.question: When shooting, where should you usually aim?
options: Right at the goalkeeper
Wide of the goal
Corners of the net
Over the goal
questions.explanation: Aim for corners because they're hardest for goalkeepers to reach.

questions.question: The best part of your foot for a powerful shot is:
options: Inside of foot
Outside edge
Toe
Top of your foot (laces)
questions.explanation: Using the top of your foot (laces) gives you the most power.

questions.question: What should you do right after shooting?
options: Start celebrating before the keeper reacts
Stand still and watch the shot
Follow up for rebounds
Turn away from the goalmouth
questions.explanation: Always follow your shot to be ready for rebounds or loose balls.

questions.question: A good first touch before shooting helps you:
options: Move the ball out of shooting range
Set up the ball for an easier shot
Hide the ball from your support players
Slow down even when space is open
questions.explanation: A clean first touch sets up an accurate and powerful shot.

questions.question: You are close to goal with an open corner to aim at. What matters most?
options: A controlled finish with enough pace to reach the gap
Maximum power regardless of direction
Making the shot as soft as possible
Lifting every shot high
questions.explanation: Accuracy and suitable pace matter more than power alone. The right finish depends on the keeper, angle, and pressure.

questions.question: Which foot should you practice shooting with?
options: Only your strong foot
Only your weak foot
Both feet
Neither
questions.explanation: Practicing with both feet makes you more dangerous and unpredictable.

questions.question: Shooting low is often good because:
options: Goalkeepers must get down quickly
Low shots cannot miss the target
Low shots always beat defenders
The keeper cannot dive sideways
questions.explanation: Low shots are harder for keepers because they must get down quickly.

questions.question: If you're off-balance, you should:
options: Shoot anyway without control
Pass or control first
Let yourself fall before deciding
Dribble away from goal every time
questions.explanation: Controlling or passing might be better if you're not balanced for a good shot.

questions.question: You have time, balance, and a clear corner to aim for. Why might you use the inside of your foot?
options: It can give good control for a placed finish
It guarantees a goal if the keeper is close
It makes checking the keeper unnecessary
It is only allowed inside the penalty area
questions.explanation: The inside of the foot can help you place a shot accurately. Use enough pace and choose a finish that fits the chance.

questions.question: The goalkeeper has caught your shot securely. What should you do?
options: Stop challenging for the ball and get ready to defend
Kick at the ball while it is in their hands
Charge into the keeper to create a rebound
Stand in their way to stop them releasing it
questions.explanation: Follow a loose rebound, but do not challenge a keeper who controls the ball with their hands. Get ready for the next phase.

questions.question: The near side is covered and the far corner is open. Why might you shoot across the keeper?
options: The open far side may be harder for them to reach
The far side is always the best choice
An across-goal shot cannot go wide
The keeper is not allowed to dive across
questions.explanation: The best target depends on the keeper and defenders. Across goal can be useful when that space is open, not on every shot.

questions.question: Before shooting, you should always:
options: Check where the goalkeeper is
Ignore the keeper and shoot blind
Turn away from goal first
Only look at the ball carrier
questions.explanation: Knowing the keeper's position helps you decide where to shoot.

questions.question: When should you shoot with your weaker foot?
options: Never, even when it is the open side
When it gives you the best quick chance
On every shot regardless of angle
Only after stopping the ball completely
questions.explanation: Use your weaker foot when needed; practice makes it better.

questions.question: A teammate has a clearer shot and the pass to them is open. What is often a good choice?
options: Pass so they can finish
Shoot from the worse angle to avoid sharing
Wait until the pass is blocked
Pass behind them to slow their run
questions.explanation: Use the player with the better chance when the pass is on. No pass guarantees a goal, but it can improve the opportunity.

questions.question: If your shot misses, you should:
options: Stop playing the next phase
Get back quickly and keep playing
Stay offside near the goal
Argue instead of recovering
questions.explanation: Mistakes happen-stay focused and ready for the next chance.

questions.question: When a teammate cuts the ball back from the endline, where should an attacker arrive?
options: Around the penalty spot or open space behind defenders
Inside their own goal
Outside the attacking third
Behind the passer only
questions.explanation: Cutbacks are dangerous because defenders often run toward their goal and leave space behind them.

questions.question: What is often better than shooting from a bad angle?
options: Pass across goal to an open teammate
Shoot into the side net from anywhere
Turn away from goal
Stop the attack
questions.explanation: A pass to a teammate with a better angle can create a much easier goal.

questions.question: Why should attackers stay calm in front of goal?
options: Calm players pick better shots
Calm players never shoot
It makes the keeper bigger
It slows the ball
questions.explanation: Composure helps you see the keeper, the corners, and open teammates.

questions.question: If the goalkeeper spills a shot, what should nearby attackers do?
options: Attack the rebound
Stop outside the box
Wait for the keeper to reset
Recover to midfield immediately
questions.explanation: Rebounds are great scoring chances because the keeper may be out of position.

questions.question: What does 'shoot across the keeper' mean?
options: Aim toward the far side of the goal from your shooting angle
Aim straight at the nearest post every time
Pass behind yourself to a supporting player
Shoot directly toward the keeper's body
questions.explanation: It describes the direction of the shot. It can create a chance or rebound, but choose the target based on the space you see.

questions.question: You receive near goal on your weaker-foot side. A defender will block you if you take another touch. What should guide the choice?
options: Whether you can make a controlled first-time finish now
Whether using your preferred foot matters more than the open chance
Whether every first-time shot is better than a pass
Whether a powerful swing can replace balance
questions.explanation: A weaker-foot finish may use an opening before it closes. Read the ball, the target, and your balance; first-time shooting is not always the answer.

questions.question: A low cutback is coming. Defenders have run toward the goal line. Where might a late arriving attacker find space?
options: Behind those defenders, in a clear lane for the cutback
Alongside the defenders on the goal line
Directly behind the passer outside their view
In the same lane as the attacker already receiving
questions.explanation: A late run can reach space defenders have left behind. Arrive in time to meet the pass rather than standing there so early that you are marked.

questions.question: The keeper steps forward and narrows your shooting angle. A teammate is free across goal with a clear pass. What should you weigh?
options: Whether the pass gives a clearer finish than your own shot
Whether the keeper moving forward requires a chip
Whether keeping the shot on your stronger foot matters most
Whether every pass across goal is intercepted
questions.explanation: Do not choose a finish by habit. Compare the available shot with the teammate's chance, including the risk and timing of the pass.

questions.question: A defender blocks the direct shooting lane, but you have space to touch sideways. Why might that touch help?
options: It can change the shooting angle before the defender adjusts
It adds power without changing the angle
It guarantees that the keeper cannot see the ball
It removes the need to check for a second defender
questions.explanation: A small touch can open a lane. Keep it controlled and check whether the extra touch gives another defender time to close you.

questions.question: A teammate shoots across goal. You are onside when the shot is taken and near the far side. What useful run can you make?
options: Follow into a reachable rebound lane without crowding the shooter
Stay still until the keeper has recovered
Run behind the goal to receive the ball
Move into the shooter's path before they strike
questions.explanation: An across-goal shot can produce a loose rebound. Anticipate it while staying aware of offside and avoiding contact with a keeper controlling the ball.
